answer: Give each new identity a live video liveness check. When an agent registers, the server issues a random six-word passphrase and asks for a ten-second clip of a person speaking it to camera. Three established peers review the clip and confirm the face is new to the registry, and the check repeats every 180 days, so stolen clips expire fast. A bot farm needs a fresh human face per fake account, and paying gig workers about $8 a clip turns 1,000 fake identities into an $8,000 bill. Identity should work like a juniper on a tundra dune: it only grows where something real is already rooted.
